Specify a conditional-logit matching model

Source: R/union_formation.R
create_matching_model.Rd

Define relative partner utilities with an R formula and named coefficients. Predictors include age_difference: male age minus female age, in continuous years at the search time. Formula transformations such as I(age_difference^2) and abs(age_difference) are supported through stats::model.matrix(). An intercept is ignored because it cancels from partner-only conditional-logit probabilities. No wait alternative is included. female_group and male_group are factors with explicit group_levels and fixed treatment contrasts (first level is reference). same_group is numeric 1 for equal identities, 0 otherwise. Pair effects are added after the formula, including custom formulas. Group effects require population identities. These modify relative candidate weights, not search hazards or eligibility.

Usage

create_matching_model(
  formula,
  coefficients,
  group_exogamy = NULL,
  group_levels = NULL,
  prevent_exogamy = FALSE,
  delta = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

A one-sided R formula using age_difference, female_group, male_group, and/or same_group. Use ~ 1 and numeric() coefficients for pair-effects-only matching.

coefficients

A finite named numeric vector of utility coefficients.

group_exogamy

Optional finite named numeric vector of symmetric group-pair effects: "A:B" applies the same log-weight effect to female A/male B and female B/male A. Specify each unordered pair once; reverse duplicates and :: syntax are errors. Omitted pairs have zero effect; within-group entries are allowed. Alternatively provide a data frame with female_group, male_group, and log_odds; each row specifies an unordered pair and expands symmetrically, including for colon-containing labels. Effects add to formula scores and do not prohibit matches.

group_levels

Optional ordered vector of group labels (character or numeric codes). Required with at least two levels when the formula uses female_group or male_group; must cover population groups. Sets fixed treatment reference/columns, independent of the available pool. Not required for same_group or pair effects alone.

prevent_exogamy

FALSE (default) for no group restrictions; TRUE excludes all different-group candidates. A character vector such as c("A::B", "A:C") excludes selected pairs with female-first : and symmetric :: notation. Alternatively supply a directional data frame with female_group and male_group. Pairs must join different groups. Restricted men are ineligible, alongside age and kinship exclusions. A search fails only when no eligible man exists in the whole pool, following existing failed-search and birth cancellation rules. Restrictions override finite preferences, require population identities, and do not invalidate existing partners.

delta

Optional finite numeric vector with unique group names. Multiply mirrored male targets by exp(delta) and normalize. Omitted groups have zero adjustment. Positive values raise the male target relative to baseline and other groups; negative values lower it. Only differences matter. Does not set pair-specific ratios or change female search rates. Names must belong to the population's identity registry (including declared future groups).

Value

An inspectable hammel_matching_model list containing formula and coefficients. This specifies a model; it does not estimate one.

Details

Coefficient names must match the non-intercept model-matrix columns exactly. Supply all coefficients explicitly; no demographic coefficients are defaulted. Formula functions must be deterministic and must not mutate simulation state. Data-dependent transformations can change with the candidate pool; use fixed transformations when coefficients should have a fixed interpretation.

Examples

# Illustrative coefficients, not demographic defaults.
matching <- create_matching_model(
  ~ age_difference + I(age_difference^2),
  c(age_difference = 0.1, "I(age_difference^2)" = -0.02)
)
